ResponseSpec:
Templates below preserve the English text sent to the model. `${…}` marks runtime substitutions, not brief template syntax.

### Final-answer format

Passing `response` to dispatch appends this block after the rendered brief and any steering messages collected at the start of the turn. This also applies to continuation, fork and repair turns. The contract overrides conflicting answer-format instructions while retaining the task instructions.

```text
Final response format:
If earlier instructions specify a conflicting response format, use this format instead. Keep following the task instructions.
End your answer with exactly one <${tag}>...</${tag}> block. Do not write anything after the closing tag.
```

`tag` comes from the response contract. For `format: "text"`, the next line is:

```text
Put the requested text inside the response tag.
```

For `format: "json"`, the following text and the input schema are appended:

```text
Put valid JSON inside the response tag, without a Markdown code fence. The JSON must conform to this input schema:
${schemaJSON}
```

`schemaJSON` is `JSON.stringify(schema, null, 2)` for the captured input JSON Schema. With `format` omitted, only the common block is sent. These additions are not expanded as brief variables or shell commands.

There is no option to replace or disable this wording while keeping `response`. `tag`, `format` and `jsonSchema` change its dynamic content. A dispatch without `response` receives none of these format instructions.

### Response repair

When `read()` throws `ResponseError`, a repair attempt is available and the failed turn has a conversation ID, dispatch resumes that conversation with this message instead of the original brief:

```text
Correct the response inside <${tag}> and </${tag}>.
Validation failure: ${error.message}
Previous content: ${previousContent}
Cause: ${cause}
Further repair attempts after this one: ${remainingAttempts}.
Do not edit files, run commands or continue implementation. Only return the corrected response.
```

`previousContent` is `error.raw`, falling back to `No complete tagged response was returned.`. `cause` is the cause's error message, otherwise its JSON serialization, falling back to `unspecified`. `remainingAttempts` counts repairs available after the new attempt. The final-answer block above is appended again, after any steering messages collected for that turn.

`repairs` controls the attempt count; it does not replace the repair prompt. `repairs: 0` disables repair turns. The built-in harness exposes only read-only tools during a repair; the instruction itself does not enforce a filesystem restriction for every CLI agent.

Implementation: [response-instructions.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/domain/response-instructions.ts) · [execution.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/execution.ts) · [steering-turns.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/steering-turns.ts).

Les templates ci-dessous conservent le texte anglais envoyé au modèle. `${…}` désigne les valeurs insérées à l’exécution, pas la syntaxe des variables d’un brief.

### Format de réponse finale

Passer `response` à un dispatch ajoute ce bloc après le brief rendu et les messages de steering recueillis au début du tour. Cela vaut aussi pour les continuations, forks et réparations. Le contrat remplace les consignes de format contradictoires tout en conservant les instructions de la tâche.

```text
Final response format:
If earlier instructions specify a conflicting response format, use this format instead. Keep following the task instructions.
End your answer with exactly one <${tag}>...</${tag}> block. Do not write anything after the closing tag.
```

`tag` vient du contrat de réponse. Avec `format: "text"`, la ligne suivante est ajoutée :

```text
Put the requested text inside the response tag.
```

Avec `format: "json"`, Outpost ajoute ce texte et le schéma d’entrée :

```text
Put valid JSON inside the response tag, without a Markdown code fence. The JSON must conform to this input schema:
${schemaJSON}
```

`schemaJSON` correspond à `JSON.stringify(schema, null, 2)` pour le JSON Schema d’entrée capturé. Si `format` est absent, seul le bloc commun est envoyé. Ces ajouts ne sont pas interprétés comme des variables de brief ou des commandes shell.

Aucune option ne permet de remplacer ou désactiver cette formulation en conservant `response`. `tag`, `format` et `jsonSchema` modifient son contenu dynamique. Un dispatch sans `response` ne reçoit aucune de ces consignes de format.

### Réparation de réponse

Lorsque `read()` lève `ResponseError`, qu’une tentative de réparation reste disponible et que le tour possède un identifiant de conversation, le dispatch reprend cette conversation avec ce message à la place du brief initial :

```text
Correct the response inside <${tag}> and </${tag}>.
Validation failure: ${error.message}
Previous content: ${previousContent}
Cause: ${cause}
Further repair attempts after this one: ${remainingAttempts}.
Do not edit files, run commands or continue implementation. Only return the corrected response.
```

`previousContent` vaut `error.raw`, ou `No complete tagged response was returned.` si cette valeur est absente. `cause` est le message de l’exception à l’origine de l’erreur, sinon sa sérialisation JSON, sinon `unspecified`. `remainingAttempts` compte les réparations encore possibles après la nouvelle tentative. Le bloc de format final ci-dessus est ajouté de nouveau, après les éventuels messages de steering recueillis pour ce tour.

`repairs` règle le nombre de tentatives, sans remplacer le prompt de réparation. `repairs: 0` désactive ces tours. Le harness intégré n’expose que les outils en lecture seule pendant une réparation ; la consigne ne constitue pas à elle seule une restriction du système de fichiers pour tous les agents CLI.

Implémentation : [response-instructions.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/domain/response-instructions.ts) · [execution.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/execution.ts) · [steering-turns.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/steering-turns.ts).
summarizeHistory:
Templates below preserve the English text sent to the model. `${…}` marks runtime substitutions, not brief template syntax.

When compaction triggers, Outpost sends this system instruction to the active agent model in a separate summary request:

```text
Summarize this earlier part of an agent conversation for the agent that will continue it. Keep the task, decisions, files and commands involved, results, errors and open questions. Be factual and concise.
```

The user prompt contains the older messages, separated by blank lines. Each message starts with `User:
` or `Assistant:
`. Text blocks are kept; tool calls become `[tool call ${name} ${inputJSON}]`; results become `[tool result]
${content}` or `[tool error]
${content}`. Reasoning blocks are omitted. An empty message list is rendered as `(no earlier messages)`.

The result is inserted into the effective history as a user message, after the first message and before the retained recent messages:

```text
Summary of the earlier conversation:
${summary}
```

The summary instruction and prefix are fixed. `triggerCharacters` and `keepRecentMessages` control when and how much to summarize. A custom [context strategy](../defineharnesscontextstrategy/) can replace the compaction mechanism, but calling `input.summarize()` still uses this fixed instruction. The built-in summary request counts toward usage and budgets.

Implementation: [context.constants.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/domain/context.constants.ts) · [harness-context.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/harness-context.ts) · [context.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/domain/context.ts).

Lorsque la réduction de l’historique se déclenche, Outpost envoie cette instruction système au modèle actif de l’agent dans une requête de résumé distincte :

```text
Summarize this earlier part of an agent conversation for the agent that will continue it. Keep the task, decisions, files and commands involved, results, errors and open questions. Be factual and concise.
```

Le prompt utilisateur contient les anciens messages, séparés par des lignes vides. Chaque message commence par `User:
` ou `Assistant:
`. Les blocs de texte sont conservés ; les appels d’outils deviennent `[tool call ${name} ${inputJSON}]` ; les résultats deviennent `[tool result]
${content}` ou `[tool error]
${content}`. Les blocs de raisonnement sont omis. Une liste de messages vide devient `(no earlier messages)`.

Le résultat est inséré dans l’historique effectif comme message utilisateur, après le premier message et avant les messages récents conservés :

```text
Summary of the earlier conversation:
${summary}
```

L’instruction de résumé et son préfixe sont fixes. `triggerCharacters` et `keepRecentMessages` règlent le déclenchement et la quantité d’historique à résumer. Une [stratégie de contexte personnalisée](../defineharnesscontextstrategy/) peut remplacer le mécanisme, mais appeler `input.summarize()` utilise toujours cette instruction fixe. La requête de résumé intégrée compte dans l’usage et les budgets.

Templates below preserve the English text sent to the model. `${…}` marks runtime substitutions, not brief template syntax.

When an older tool result exceeds `maxCharacters`, its content is replaced with:

```text
${retainedContent}
[earlier output truncated from ${originalLength} characters]
```

`retainedContent` is the first `maxCharacters` JavaScript string code units; `originalLength` is the original string's `length`. This is a marker in the tool result, not a separate model request. Its wording is fixed. Change `maxCharacters` or `keepRecent` to control truncation, or supply a custom context strategy to use another transformation.

Implementation: [context.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/domain/context.ts).

Quand un ancien résultat d’outil dépasse `maxCharacters`, son contenu est remplacé par :

```text
${retainedContent}
[earlier output truncated from ${originalLength} characters]
```

`retainedContent` contient les `maxCharacters` premières unités de code de la chaîne JavaScript ; `originalLength` est la propriété `length` de la chaîne initiale. Ce marqueur appartient au résultat d’outil et ne déclenche aucun appel au modèle. Sa formulation est fixe. QuotaResumePolicy:
Templates below preserve the English text sent to the model. `${…}` marks runtime substitutions, not brief template syntax.

Automatic continuation after a quota pause replaces the original brief with:

```text
Your previous turn was interrupted by a usage or rate limit before it finished. Continue the same task from where you stopped. Inspect the workspace first: changes that were not committed may be missing.
```

For ordinary agent tasks with a response tag, this line follows:

```text
Return the final answer inside <${tag}> and </${tag}>.
```

Dispatch then appends the complete [response-format instructions](../responsespec/#outpost-instructions). Interactive tasks use the same base quota message followed by their [dialogue protocol](../defineinteractiveagenttask/#outpost-instructions).

For ordinary tasks, this replacement requires `quotaResume: "continue"` (the default), a captured quota conversation, a resumable non-fallback agent, one pass and no explicit `continuation` in the request. Otherwise the requested brief is kept. A fallback agent restarts with the original brief. Interactive tasks manage their quota continuation internally and do not expose `quotaResume`.

The resume text cannot be overridden. `quotaResume: "restart"` selects the original request instead of this automatic continuation; it does not edit the resume message.

Implementation: [quota-resume.constants.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/quota-resume.constants.ts) · [quota-resume.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/quota-resume.ts).

Les templates ci-dessous conservent le texte anglais envoyé au modèle. `${…}` désigne les valeurs insérées à l’exécution, pas la syntaxe des variables d’un brief.

La continuation automatique après une pause de quota remplace le brief initial par :

```text
Your previous turn was interrupted by a usage or rate limit before it finished. Continue the same task from where you stopped. Inspect the workspace first: changes that were not committed may be missing.
```

Pour les tâches d’agent ordinaires avec une balise de réponse, cette ligne suit :

```text
Return the final answer inside <${tag}> and </${tag}>.
```

Le dispatch ajoute ensuite les [consignes complètes de format de réponse](../responsespec/#outpost-instructions). Les tâches interactives utilisent le même message de base, suivi de leur [protocole de dialogue](../defineinteractiveagenttask/#outpost-instructions).

Pour les tâches ordinaires, ce remplacement exige `quotaResume: "continue"` (le défaut), une conversation capturée lors du quota, un agent reprenable sans repli, une seule passe et aucune `continuation` explicite dans la requête. Sinon, le brief demandé est conservé. Un agent de repli redémarre avec le brief initial. Les tâches interactives gèrent leur continuation après quota en interne et n’exposent pas `quotaResume`.

Le texte de reprise n’est pas remplaçable. `quotaResume: "restart"` sélectionne la requête initiale au lieu de cette continuation automatique ; il ne modifie pas le message de reprise.

createAgentConflictResolver:
Templates below preserve the English text sent to the model. `${…}` marks runtime substitutions, not brief template syntax.

After preparing the conflicting merge in the separate resolution workspace, the resolver sends this literal brief to its agent:

```text
Resolve the pending Git merge in this workspace. Candidate commit: ${candidateCommit}. Host commit: ${hostCommit}.
Conflicting paths: ${conflictsJSON}. Preserve the intent of both branches.
Resolve every unmerged entry, stage the resolution and commit the merge. Do not abort the merge, rewrite history, change other branches or weaken tests to make them pass.
${instructions}
```

`candidateCommit` and `hostCommit` are the frozen source and host commits from `ConflictContext`. `conflictsJSON` is `JSON.stringify(context.conflicts)`. `instructions` is `options.instructions`, or an empty string; it is appended without variable or command expansion.

`instructions` adds guidance and does not replace the built-in text. A custom [ConflictResolver](../conflictresolver/) can replace the whole strategy. Verification, ancestry checks and workspace guards are enforced separately from the prompt. A conflict-free merge does not invoke this agent.

Implementation: [agent-conflict-resolver.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/agent-conflict-resolver.ts).

```text
Conflicting paths: ${conflictsJSON}. Preserve the intent of both branches.
Resolve every unmerged entry, stage the resolution and commit the merge. Do not abort the merge, rewrite history, change other branches or weaken tests to make them pass.
${instructions}
```

`instructions` complète les consignes sans remplacer le texte intégré. Un [ConflictResolver](../conflictresolver/) personnalisé peut remplacer la stratégie entière. La vérification, les contrôles d’ascendance et les garde-fous du workspace sont imposés séparément du prompt. Une fusion sans conflit n’appelle pas cet agent.

defineHarnessSkill:
Templates below preserve the English text sent to the model. `${…}` marks runtime substitutions, not brief template syntax.

When `createHarness({ skills })` receives a nonempty skill list, it adds this catalog to the system instructions after profile and harness instructions, before session-start hook additions:

```text
Skills are available on demand. Call load_skill with a skill name to read its instructions and enable its tools before using them:
- ${skill.name}: ${skill.description}
```

The name/description line repeats for each skill in declaration order. The injected `load_skill` tool has this model-visible description:

```text
Load a skill listed in the instructions: returns its instructions and enables its tools for the following steps.
```

Loading a skill resolves its instructions and returns them as tool output. If the skill has tools, the output is:

```text
${resolvedInstructions}

Tools now available: ${toolNames}.
```

`toolNames` joins the skill's tool names with `, `. Without tools, only `resolvedInstructions` is returned. Loading does not append the skill body to the system prompt.

Skill names, descriptions and instruction sources are configurable. The catalog introduction, loader description and tool-availability suffix are fixed; there is no override option. Omitting skills removes this machinery. Whether tools stay unlocked is determined from the effective history, so compaction can require loading a skill again.

Implementation: [skill.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/domain/skill.ts) · [harness.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/domain/harness.ts) · [harness-loop.ts](https://gitlab.elielaloum.com/elielaloum/outpost/-/blob/main/src/application/harness-loop.ts).

Les templates ci-dessous conservent le texte anglais envoyé au modèle. `${…}` désigne les valeurs insérées à l’exécution, pas la syntaxe des variables d’un brief.

Quand `createHarness({ skills })` reçoit une liste non vide, il ajoute ce catalogue aux instructions système après celles du profil et du harness, avant les ajouts des hooks session-start :

```text
Skills are available on demand. Call load_skill with a skill name to read its instructions and enable its tools before using them:
- ${skill.name}: ${skill.description}
```

La ligne nom/description est répétée pour chaque compétence dans l’ordre de déclaration. L’outil injecté `load_skill` porte cette description visible par le modèle :

```text
Load a skill listed in the instructions: returns its instructions and enables its tools for the following steps.
```

Charger une compétence résout ses instructions et les renvoie comme résultat d’outil. Si la compétence possède des outils, ce résultat est :

```text
${resolvedInstructions}

Tools now available: ${toolNames}.
```

`toolNames` joint les noms des outils de la compétence avec `, `. Sans outils, seul `resolvedInstructions` est renvoyé. Le chargement n’ajoute pas le corps de la compétence au prompt système.

Les noms, descriptions et sources d’instructions sont configurables. L’introduction du catalogue, la description du chargeur et le suffixe annonçant les outils sont fixes ; aucune option ne permet de les remplacer. Omettre les compétences retire ce mécanisme. Le déverrouillage des outils dépend de l’historique effectif ; une réduction de l’historique peut donc imposer de recharger une compétence.
